analysis.title: UBS Europe Equity Weekly
key_insights: AI de-risking is the dominant flow in European tech, but valuations already discount a large earnings reset. ASML (Buy, PT €2,400), STM (Buy, PT €80) and NXP (Neutral, PT USD 270) are the most de-risked names, with current valuations implying more than 50% cuts to UBS 2028E AI earnings. ASML implies about 57% downside versus UBS estimates.
ASM International (Buy, PT €1,380 from €1,325) is a company-specific growth story. UBS forecasts €6bn revenue in 2027 (+38%) and almost €8bn in 2028.

The AI debate is moving down the infrastructure stack. UBS prefers Siemens Energy, Halma, Munters, Nexans, Schneider Electric and Prysmian after the sell-off. Clients question returns per GW and whether hyperscaler capex can keep accelerating.
Munters (Buy, PT SEK210 from SEK245) has a SEK23bn backlog despite near-term execution issues. Prysmian (Buy, PT €175) delivered a 7% EBITDA beat and raised FY26 guidance.

UBS favours self-help and pricing stories in European industrials over a broad macro recovery. Rockwool (Buy, PT DKr265) could deliver about 9% 2027 pricing including carry-over, while 4-5% offsets cost inflation. At 9% pricing UBS estimates €150-160m of positive price-cost versus about €46m of EBIT growth embedded in consensus.

Holcim (Buy, PT CHF93) is supported by pricing, with investor feedback about 80/20 bull/bear after results. Saint-Gobain (Sell, PT €65) is challenged: Q3 volumes fell 0.7%, France weakened and price-cost is less supportive. UBS FY26/27 EPS forecasts are about 3%/4% below consensus.
Assa Abloy (Buy, PT SEK450) and KONE (Buy, PT €67) remain preferred idiosyncratic compounders.

DSV (Buy, PT DKr1,805) is becoming an execution story. Q3 gave the first evidence that the Schenker integration is stabilising: road on-time delivery reached 94% and more than 60% of groupage costs are fixed. DSV expects YoY Air & Sea volume growth to return in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027.

DSV valuation: UBS forecasts EPS rising from DKr57.8 in 2026 to DKr88.3 in 2028 and DKr105 in 2030. DSV trades at about 15.5x FY28E EPS versus about 22x for Kuehne+Nagel. About DKr10.7bn of working capital offers cash-release potential, and the case assumes flat Air & Sea gross profit through 2028.

European banks are posting strong numbers, but investors want bigger earnings upgrades. BNP Paribas (Buy, PT €119) had revenues 2% ahead, adjusted PBT about 4% above consensus, CIB pre-provision profit 11% ahead and a new €1.3bn buyback. It trades at about 6.7x 2027E P/E.

Standard Chartered (Neutral, PT 2,188p) beat PBT by 12% and raised FY26 ROTE guidance to about 14%. HSBC (Neutral, PT 1,501p) was softer, with Banking NII 2% below consensus and Wealth PBT 10% below UBSe.

UBS remains constructive on beverages. AB InBev (Buy, PT €90) had +0.4% organic volumes despite China -16.8%, +4.5% price/mix and a 6% EPS beat. Heineken (Buy, PT €89) reported about 4% volume growth. Carlsberg (Buy, PT DKr1,100) offers China normalisation, soft-drinks growth and potential FY27 buybacks.

Campari (Buy, PT €7.20) is improving, with Europe +7.7% organically and US sell-out turning positive. Danone (Buy, PT €93) is preferred in Food/HPC, with +3.6% pricing absorbing inflation and volume/mix positive.

Unilever (Sell, PT 4,390p) has Q3 volumes beating, but Foods is weak, comparisons get tougher and UBS sees another €700m-€1bn of input-cost inflation in 2027. Haleon (Buy, PT 478p) had a top-line reset but retains productivity, deleveraging and a new £0.5bn buyback.

European energy cash returns surprised positively. Shell (Neutral, PT 4,100p) announced a $5bn quarterly buyback versus $3.5-4bn expected. Repsol (Neutral, PT €30) announced up to €950m. Eni (Buy, PT €32 from €30) added a €1.3bn special dividend and raised buybacks to €3.8bn.

Galp (Buy, PT €24 from €25) beat Q3 EBITDA by 3% and operating cash flow ex-working capital by 14%, and raised FY26 EBITDA guidance to about €5bn from €4bn. The failed Moeve transaction erased about €1.8bn of market value. UBS sees about €750m of potential 2027 buybacks and a 9.6% organic FCF yield, but management credibility is part of the debate.

Genmab (Buy, PT DKr3,100) is a high-conviction long after ESMO. Petosemtamab showed 75%/67% ORR in first-/second-line colorectal cancer, and Rina-S has an estimated PFS of about 12 months in ovarian cancer. UBS models $4bn unadjusted peak sales for petosemtamab in H&N.

Novartis (Neutral, PT CHF116) has the opposite setup. Remibrutinib relapse reductions were 35%/31% versus 51%/59% for fenebrutinib on a cross-trial basis, though clean liver safety preserves UBS's $3.5bn RMS peak-sales view. Hedge funds are positioned long and Q3 was seen as a low-quality beat-and-raise.
Straumann (Buy, PT CHF115) remains preferred into 2027 on North American share gains, China VBP de-risking and potential margin upside.

ESMO: Roche divarasib (Buy, PT CHF376) showed median PFS of 9.8 vs 5.7 months and OS of 17.7 vs 12.0 months versus first-generation KRAS inhibitors in previously treated KRAS G12C NSCLC. Roche raised its peak-sales ambition to CHF2-3bn.

AstraZeneca (Buy, PT 15,200p) readouts: Imfinzi + Imdelltra cut death risk 58% in SCLC, Sone-Ve doubled median OS to 10 months in 3L+ gastric cancer, and VOLGA cut death risk 42% in bladder cancer. AVANZAR has moved to Q1 2027. GSK Mo-Rez (Neutral, PT 1,940p) showed 62% ORR and about 11 months PFS.

Transport: UBS forecasts 4.9% global airline traffic growth in 2027 and airline profits recovering from about $25bn in 2026 to about $38bn, with downside risk if fuel stays elevated. Ryanair (Buy, PT €30) and Lufthansa (Buy, PT €10) are preferred.

The UK Budget helps Whitbread (Buy, PT 3,150p): business-rate relief could cut a previously expected £110m incremental cost by more than half. UBS sees French and Italian sovereign spreads as a cross-asset risk into 2027.

Stock reactions depend on expectations x positioning x credibility, not just beats and misses. Rockwool entered with light positioning, Shell's crowded positioning mattered less after a larger buyback, and clients are increasingly willing to engage with the AI downside case.

earnings_insights: Prysmian (reported Q3): EBITDA 7% above consensus, Electrification about 20% ahead, FY26 EBITDA guidance raised to €3.075-3.125bn.
Inficon (reported Q3): sales 13% and EBIT 38% above consensus, record Semiconductor orders, materially higher guidance.
SIG Group (reported Q3): LFL sales +6.5% versus +3.6% consensus, EBIT 12% ahead, medium-term margin target raised to above 18%.
AB InBev (reported Q3): volumes +0.4% versus +0.3% consensus, price/mix +4.5% versus +3.8%, EPS 6% above consensus. China volumes fell 16.8%.
Orange (reported Q3): revenue +1.3% and EBITDAaL +0.9% versus consensus, plus another FY26 guidance upgrade.
BNP Paribas (reported Q3): revenues 2% ahead, adjusted PBT about 4% above consensus, CIB pre-provision profit 11% ahead, €1.3bn buyback.
Standard Chartered (reported): adjusted PBT 12% above consensus, FY26 ROTE guidance raised to about 14%.
HSBC (reported Q3): income 2% below and pre-provision profit 3% below expectations, Banking NII 2% below consensus, Wealth PBT 10% below UBSe. Better impairments left adjusted PBT broadly in line.
Shell (reported Q3): $5bn quarterly buyback versus $3.5-4bn expected. Repsol: net income about 4% ahead, buyback up to €950m. Eni: €1.3bn special dividend and buybacks raised to €3.8bn.
Galp (reported Q3): EBITDA 3% ahead, operating cash flow ex-working capital 14% ahead, FY26 EBITDA guidance raised to about €5bn from €4bn.
STM (reported): revenue and opex slightly soft, gross margins better.
Danone (reported Q3): LFL +4.0% versus +3.7% consensus, driven by pricing. Campari: organic sales broadly in line.

Airbus (reported): revenue missed by 2.5%, EBIT in line, FCF slightly weak, guidance unchanged. KONE: adjusted EBITA 2.4% below consensus. Renault: essentially in line, margin guidance of 5.3-5.7% maintained.
Unilever (reported Q3): volumes +2.9% versus +2.5% consensus. Foods weak.

Haleon (reported): FY26 growth guidance lowered and EPS cut. Reckitt: core LFL +3.3% versus +4.1% consensus, guidance lowered. Adyen: lower 2026 EBITDA-margin guidance and withdrawal of the above-55% 2028 target.
Saint-Gobain (reported Q3): volumes negative (-0.7%), France weaker. Munters: DCT execution and margins disappointed, 2026 adjusted EBITA cut 10%.
